Article Title: Nestle dairy whitener found unsafe, substandard by FSSAI; Nestle says product safe
Article Text:
A Nestlé India spokesperson said phosphorus occurs naturally in milk and is therefore present in milk-based products

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: A sample of Nestlé India’s Low Fat Dairy Whitener, collected from the premises of The LaLiT in Connaught Place, has been declared “unsafe and substandard” by a Food Analyst’s laboratory, the Food Safety and Standards Authority of India (FSSAI) said on Saturday.The sample was collected from M/s Bharat Hotels Ltd (The LaLiT), Connaught Place, FSSAI said. The regulator said the Food Analyst’s report found the product non-compliant under the Food Safety and Standards Act, 2006.FSSAI said a copy of the laboratory analysis report was provided to the food business operator and a notice was issued regarding the non-compliant product. The operator was given an opportunity to appeal against the Food Analyst’s report within the prescribed period. FSSAI also directed that the identified product be immediately prohibited from sale.However, Nestlé India said the product is safe to consume and complies with all applicable regulatory requirements.A Nestlé India spokesperson said phosphorus occurs naturally in milk and is therefore present in milk-based products. The company said the FSSAI laboratory report reflects total phosphorus against the additive limit without accounting for the substantial natural phosphorus contribution from milk-based ingredients.Nestlé said the product is in full compliance with prescribed limits for added phosphorus under the Food Safety and Standards Regulations, including on an “as consumed” basis. The company said it has been engaging with the authorities through the due process established under law and has shared data on other same or similar milk-based products to demonstrate the presence of naturally occurring phosphorus.The LaLiT said the product was a packaged product procured from Nestlé India and that the sample was collected by FSSAI from the hotel approximately three months ago.Vivek Shukla, CEO, The LaLiT Suri Hospitality Group, said that after receiving communication from FSSAI, the hotel immediately took up the matter with Nestlé India, which assured it that the company would respond directly to FSSAI.The hotel said it simultaneously discontinued use of the product and removed all packets from its operations.“The matter concerning the product’s compliance is between FSSAI and Nestlé India and not with The LaLiT,” Shukla said, adding that the hotel had acted promptly after receiving the communication and remained committed to food safety protocols and compliance with FSSAI regulations.FSSAI’s public communication does not specify the particular laboratory finding or parameter that led to the sample being classified as unsafe and substandard.
Article Summary: A sample of Nestlé India’s Low Fat Dairy Whitener has been declared ‘unsafe and substandard’ The sample was collected from M/s Bharat Hotels Ltd (The LaLiT), Connaught Place. Nestlé said the product is in full compliance with prescribed limits for added phosphorus.

Article Title: Army soldier found hanging in a shed in Jammu; probe on
Article Text:
Soldier found dead at Jammu Army camp

NEW DELHI: A 45-year-old Army soldier was found hanging in a shed at the Sunjwan camp in Jammu on Sunday, news agency PTI reported citing officials.The deceased was identified as Naik Wagh Ambades, a resident of Maharashtra. Officials said he allegedly died by suicide.The reason behind the alleged suicide was not immediately known. Police have initiated inquest proceedings to ascertain the circumstances surrounding the death.His body was taken to Government Medical College Hospital in Jammu for postmortem and other legal procedures.
Article Summary: Soldier found hanging in a shed at the Sunjwan camp in Jammu on Sunday. Naik Wagh Ambades, a resident of Maharashtra, allegedly died by suicide. Police have initiated inquest proceedings to ascertain the circumstances surrounding the death.

Article Title: Punjab arms network busted: AK-47, grenades seized, accused linked to foreign smugglers
Article Text:
Image source: DGP Punjab Polic X account

NEW DELHI: Amritsar Rural Police have busted an illegal arms and explosives supply network, arresting one accused.In a post shared by the DGP Punjab Police on X, the police said the operation also resulted in the recovery of an AK-47 rifle, a magazine, live cartridges and two hand grenades.Preliminary investigation has revealed that the accused is allegedly linked to foreign-based smugglers and was involved in procuring illegal weapons, police said.An FIR has been registered at Gharinda police station in Amritsar under relevant sections of the Arms Act and Explosive Substances Act.Further investigation is underway to uncover the wider network and establish its backward and forward linkages, police said.The Punjab Police said it remained committed to maintaining strict vigil against illegal arms trafficking and organised criminal networks and taking firm action against those involved in the illegal supply chain.
Article Summary: Amritsar Rural Police have busted an illegal arms and explosives supply network. The operation also resulted in the recovery of an AK-47 rifle, a magazine, live cartridges and two hand grenades. The accused is allegedly linked to foreign- based smugglers and was involved in procuring illegal weapons.

Article Title: ‘Utterly shameful’: Tharoor slams police action against women protesters in Delhi
Article Text:
Tharoor condemns alleged police violence against women protesters

NEW DELHI: Congress leader Shashi Tharoor on Sunday criticised the alleged police action against women protesters in Delhi, saying it was “utterly shameful” that women protesting violence against women had themselves become victims of violence by policemen.“It’s utterly shameful for women protesting violence against women to become victims of violence against women by policemen!!” Tharoor said in a post on X, while sharing a video student leader by Neha Bora.In the video, Bora announced a citizens’ march from India Gate to Jantar Mantar at 3 pm on Sunday, October 4, calling for protests against the Delhi Police and the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls.“Tomorrow 3 PM. From Streets to Protests, Women Are NOT SAFE! Delhi Police's assault against women protestors, journalists will not be tolerated! In the spirit of women taking back the streets: Rise against Delhi Police! Rise against anti-women SIR! Rise for freedom. Rise against Gyanesh Kumar! Citizens' March. India Gate to Jantar Mantar 3 PM, Sunday, 4th October 2026 Jantar Mantar 2.0!”This comes as three women journalists have alleged sexual harassment by police personnel while covering a protest against Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar at Jantar Mantar on October 3, with their complaints transferred to the Crime Branch for a “fair and impartial enquiry”.The allegations have drawn criticism from journalists and opposition leaders, with the Committee to Protect Journalists (CJP) set to protest over the incident.AAP Delhi unit chief Saurabh Bharadwaj and party workers also staged a protest outside Parliament Street police station, demanding registration of an FIR.One of the journalists told PTI that an assistant commissioner of police sexually assaulted her while she was covering the protest. She alleged that police personnel were detaining protesters and that no women police personnel were present at the spot.“Police personnel were detaining protesters, and there were no women police personnel present at the spot. I asked ACP Vivek Bhagat of the Delhi Police about the absence of women police personnel, following which he sexually assaulted me and pushed me back,” she alleged.The journalist said she and others later went to a police station to lodge an FIR but alleged that no action had been taken so far.Delhi Police, however, said on Sunday that it had received complaints from three women journalists alleging sexual harassment by police personnel.“On 03-10-26, during the protest in New Delhi area, while being in law and order situation, allegations of sexual harassment were made by three female journalists against police officers. New Delhi District has received their complaints,” Delhi Police said in a post on X.The complaints were received by the New Delhi district police following the protest, during which police personnel were deployed to maintain law and order. The complaints against the police officers have been transferred to the Crime Branch at Kamla Market, which will examine the allegations and record statements of the complainants and others concerned.
Article Summary: Congress leader condemns alleged police action against women protesters in Delhi. Tharoor says it is ‘utterly shameful’ that women protesting violence against women had themselves become victims of violence by policemen. Three women journalists have alleged sexual harassment by police personnel while covering a protest.

Article Title: ‘She will continue’: Thiruvananthapuram mayor denies BJP councillor Sreelekha resigned from post
Article Text:
Rajesh had initially said he received a resignation letter from Sreelekha on September 30.

Mayor says Sreelekha will remain councillor

CPM attacks BJP councillor

Sreelekha's role in BJP

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

Thiruvananthapuram Mayor V V Rajesh on Sunday said former Kerala DGP and BJP councillor R Sreelekha would continue in office, denying that she had resigned from the Corporation.The controversy began after a message purportedly posted by Sreelekha in a WhatsApp group of residents in her ward said she had submitted her resignation to the Mayor and would give a copy to the District Collector on October 5.Rajesh had initially said he received a resignation letter from Sreelekha on September 30 but had not sent it to the Corporation Secretary, who is authorised to accept such resignations. He had also said the letter cited personal difficulties.On Sunday, however, Rajesh said there was no resignation letter."Who told you that she has given the resignation letter? She will continue and I have said it yesterday itself," he said.When asked about the WhatsApp message attributed to Sreelekha, Rajesh did not directly address it. He instead said there was no threat to the functioning of the Corporation."You want the governance to take place smoothly. As all desire, the governance will go forward strongly," he said.Rajesh said councillors often submit letters seeking funds for their wards or raising issues related to their functioning."Such a letter was given to me for the smooth operations in the ward. As she is a ruling councillor, I find that some of the matters cited in it require the party's intervention. Some have to be done by the Mayor. We will address the matters as in letters given by other councillors," he said.He said Sreelekha would remain a councillor and complete her five-year term.Sreelekha has not yet publicly responded to the conflicting statements over her alleged resignation.CPM leader and former minister V Sivankutty criticised Sreelekha and questioned her credibility."Nothing that Sreelekha says can be believed. Not only that, she will resort to any threat to secure position and power. This should only be viewed as a threat directed at the BJP to gain new positions," he said.Asked whether Sreelekha was putting pressure on the BJP with a possible move towards the Congress, Sivankutty said some politicians would move wherever they saw greater benefits."Naturally, some go where there is greater benefit. They will move to wherever they get the maximum advantage," he said.The BJP took control of the Thiruvananthapuram Corporation for the first time last year after securing the support of 51 councillors, including an Independent, in the 101-member civic body.Sreelekha was elected from the Sasthamangalam ward on a BJP ticket in last year's local body elections. She is currently the BJP's state vice president.Her continuation as a BJP councillor is significant for the party because its majority in the Corporation is narrow and depends on the support of an Independent councillor.Sreelekha also contested the Vattiyoorkavu Assembly seat in April but lost to Congress leader K Muraleedharan.
Article Summary: Thiruvananthapuram Mayor V V Rajesh on Sunday said former Kerala DGP and BJP councillor R Sreelekha would continue in office. He denied that she had resigned from the Corporation. Rajesh had initially said he received a resignation letter from SreeLekha on September 30. He had also said the letter cited personal difficulties.

Article Title: Asian Games Medal Tally: India win 8 medals but remain outside top 10 as gold continues to elude
Article Text:
Yashvir Singh, Rohit Yadav, and Esha Singh

Eight medals, but no gold for India

Shooting and kurash add to India's tally

Asian Games Medal Tally after Day 9

NEW DELHI: India produced another strong medal haul at the Asian Games 2026 on Monday, winning eight medals across athletics, shooting and kurash. However, the impressive collection did not bring any change in the overall standings, with India remaining 12th as the country continued to wait for another gold medal.India added four silver and four bronze medals during the day but could not increase its gold tally. After Day 9, India stood at 45 medals — four gold, 20 silver and 21 bronze.'The eight-medal haul included silver medals for Yashvir Singh, Murali Sreeshankar, Gulveer Singh and Esha Singh, while Rohit Yadav, Parul Chaudhary, Vithya Ramraj and Pincky Balhara won bronze.India's strongest showing came in the men's javelin, where Yashvir and Rohit produced a double podium finish in the absence of defending champion Neeraj Chopra.Yashvir recorded a personal best of 85.72m for silver, while Rohit won bronze with 84.35m. Sri Lanka's Rumesh Pathirage claimed gold with 88.55m.Sreeshankar also won silver in the men's long jump with 8.07m despite an injury forcing him to abandon his final two attempts. China's Yuhao Shi took gold with 8.17m.Gulveer added his second silver of the Games with a personal best of 3:36.72 in the men's 1500m, having earlier finished runner-up in the 10,000m.Parul Chaudhary won bronze in the women's 5000m with 15:14.61, adding to the bronze she had claimed in the 3000m steeplechase.Vithya Ramraj also took bronze in the women's 400m hurdles with a personal best of 54.75 seconds.Esha Singh secured silver in the women's 25m pistol after finishing with 38 hits, the same score as China's Xiao Jiaruixuan, who won the gold after the shoot-off.Pincky Balhara added bronze in the women's -78kg kurash category, losing 0-5 to South Korea's Sumin Mo in the semifinals.Despite the eight medals, India's gold tally remained at four, a crucial factor in the standings as countries are ranked by gold medals first.China led with 132 golds, followed by Japan with 41, South Korea with 21 and Uzbekistan with 12. India remained 12th with 45 medals, highlighting how a large haul of silver and bronze medals has yet to translate into a significant rise in the standings.
Article Summary: India added four silver and four bronze medals during the day but could not increase its gold tally. After Day 9, India stood at 45 medals — four gold, 20 silver and 21 bronze. The eight-medal haul included silver medals for Yashvir Singh, Murali Sreeshankar, Gulveer Singh and Esha Singh.

Article Title: CJP protest: Scuffle breaks out near Shiv Sena Bhavan as supporters return from stir; watch
Article Text:
A scuffle erupted near Shiv Sena Bhavan in Dadar after a protest





MUMBAI: A scuffle broke out near Shiv Sena Bhavan in Dadar after supporters of the Cockroach Janta Party (CJP) returned from a protest at Shivaji Park.A video from the spot shows protesters arguing, with some allegedly hitting each other.The situation soon turned physical, prompting police to intervene and disperse those involved. Mumbai Police later said the situation was under control and peaceful.The incident followed a CJP protest at Shivaji Park over the party’s demands concerning Chief Election Commissioner (CEC) Gyanesh Kumar.Before the protest, a Dadar resident had opposed the demonstration. “They are doing it forcefully. This protest should not take place,” the resident said, adding that such demonstrations disturb peace in the area.The CJP has been demanding Kumar’s resignation and changes to the functioning and appointment process of the Election Commission. The Election Commission currently lists Gyanesh Kumar as the Chief Election Commissioner.Mumbai Police had earlier denied permission for the CJP to hold its October 2 protest at Shivaji Park. The party later announced a “Jail Bharo Andolan”.Meanwhile, a 75-year-old Thane resident died after suffering a heart attack while attending the CJP protest at Shivaji Park on Friday evening.The deceased was identified as Gopalakrishna Subbaiya Pillai, a resident of Dosti West County in Thane.Pillai arrived at Shivaji Park around 4.30pm to attend the protest. Around 5pm, he complained of chest pain. His friend and police personnel at the spot helped take him to Sushrusha Hospital in Shivaji Park.Police personnel tried to revive him with CPR before he was taken to the hospital, where he died while undergoing treatment. Police said doctors attributed his death to a heart attack.
Article Summary: A scuffle broke out near Shiv Sena Bhavan in Dadar after supporters of the Cockroach Janta Party returned from a protest at Shivaji Park. A video from the spot shows protesters arguing, with some allegedly hitting each other. The situation soon turned physical, prompting police to intervene and disperse those involved. Mumbai Police later said the situation was under control and peaceful.

Article Title: Flydubai attack: Co-pilot identified as Hamam Alhamami was barred from flying in Oman over 'extremist views'
Article Text:
As per reports, Alhamami had repeatedly expressed support for Palestinians and hostility towards Israel. His alleged views are being examined as part of a wider investigation into possible Islamic radicalisation and terrorist motives

Removed from Oman Air training role

Pro-Palestinian material found among belongings

Questions over clearance for Tel Aviv flight

Who is Hamam Alhamami?

What happened aboard flydubai flight

The Omani co-pilot accused of attacking Indian pilot Captain Smit Machchhar aboard a flydubai flight to Tel Aviv has been identified as Hamam Alhamami. He was barred from flying in Oman over concerns about his alleged extremist views.Al Arabiya English, citing sources, reported that he had spent much of his time outside Oman, particularly in Syria, where he was allegedly influenced by extremist ideas before travelling to the UAE.The revelations follow a CNN report that Alhamami had been removed from a training role at Oman Air, Oman's national carrier, last year. However, he was later given another role at the airline, the report said, citing a regional diplomatic source familiar with the matter.Further reports have raised questions about Alhamami's alleged ideological views. i24 News, citing an Emirati source, reported that leaflets and publications from “Free Palestine” groups, along with other pro-Palestinian material, were found among his belongings.According to the report, Alhamami had repeatedly expressed support for Palestinians and hostility towards Israel. The report said investigators were examining the material as part of a broader probe into his alleged Islamic radicalisation and possible terrorist motives.The reports have also raised questions about how Alhamami was cleared to serve on a Tel Aviv-bound flight despite being an Omani citizen. Oman does not recognise Israel and has no diplomatic relations with the country.An Israeli official told CNN that several agencies, including Shin Bet, Mossad, the military and the Transportation Ministry, were investigating how Alhamami came to be part of the flight crew.According to the report, Alhamami is an Omani citizen. He was born in the United Arab Emirates to an Omani father and Syrian mother and spent several years of his life in the UAE. The Jerusalem Post, citing sources close to the investigation, reported that he did not hold a second nationality.CNN reported that Alhamami had worked for flydubai for only eight months. He had previously worked for Royal Air Maroc, Morocco's national carrier.Alhamami was transferred from Saudi Arabia to the UAE after the aircraft made an emergency landing in Tabuk. He is facing a terrorism investigation in the UAE.The September 30 incident took place aboard a flydubai flight travelling from Dubai to Tel Aviv. Alhamami allegedly attacked Captain Machchhar inside the cockpit in what is being investigated as a possible terror-driven attempt to bring down the aircraft.The confrontation triggered a steep descent, with the aircraft dropping approximately 16,000 feet within two minutes before a hijacking distress signal was transmitted.Despite suffering severe injuries, Captain Machchhar resisted the attack and managed to open the cockpit door. Flight crew members and passengers then entered the cockpit and restrained Alhamami, allowing the crew to regain control of the aircraft.Two non-duty aviators who were travelling aboard the flight also helped assume control of the aircraft. The plane subsequently made an emergency landing in Tabuk, Saudi Arabia, with all 180 occupants disembarking safely.
Article Summary: Hamam Alhamami is the Omani co-pilot accused of attacking Captain Smit Machchhar aboard a flydubai flight to Tel Aviv. He was barred from flying in Oman over concerns about his alleged extremist views. Pro-Palestinian material was found among his belongings, according to reports.

NEW DELHI: The office of the Goa chief electoral officer on Thursday said 88 of the 97 voters in the state whose names could not be included in the roll due to an alleged ECINet issue have been added back after their duly filled Form 6 was accepted. However, he also revealed that three of these 97 electors are Portuguese passport holders while six others were electors currently based outside India."In respect of voters who are currently residing outside India, officials are making efforts to establish and maintain contact with them for necessary action," the CEO said while sharing the status report on the 97 cases on X.Section 9 of the Constitution disallows dual citizenship. Goans born before 1961 in former Portuguese territories, as well as their kids and grandchildren, can apply for a Portuguese passport based on a citizen card issued by the Portuguese authorities after verifying their birth/descent documents. Portugal recognises dual citizenship; however, since dual citizenship is not allowed in India, anybody who acquires a foreign passport must surrender his Indian passport.As per Sec 9 of the Citizenship Act, 1955, a person's Indian citizenship automatically ceases upon acquiring foreign citizenship.Thus, three of the Portuguese passport holders in Goa may be classified as non-citizens, making them ineligible to be enrolled as Indian electors, said a source.Incidentally, Portuguese passport holders form 3% of the cohort of 97 electors for which the Goa CEO had repeatedly written to the EC after the ERO could not add them back via ERONet, leading the ECs to also raise questions on why access for such changes was 'centralised' and not available to the field officers. The issue was further amplified by the opposition parties after The Indian Express reported on the alleged internal notes of the election commissioners in this regard.EC sources on Thursday said the due diligence by the ERO the second time around may have served the purpose of SIR, as it is aimed at eliminating ineligible persons from the voters' list. Also, the fact that the issue was detected at the ERO level proves that the absolute right to add or delete a voter, based on verification, remains with the field officers, an EC officer told TOI.
Article Summary: 88 of the 97 voters in the state whose names could not be included in the roll due to an alleged ECINet issue have been added back after their duly filled Form 6 was accepted. Three of these 97 electors are Portuguese passport holders while six others were electors currently based outside India. Since dual citizenship is not allowed in India, anybody who acquires a foreign passport must surrender his Indian passport.

NEW DELHI: The Delhi High Court has refused to grant bail to Umar Khalid and Sharjeel Imam in the UAPA case related to the 2020 Delhi riots.Senior Advocate Trideep Pais, appearing for Umar Khalid, submitted that there had been three “small changes in circumstances” since the earlier proceedings. He also referred the court to a Supreme Court judgment in support of his submissions.Pais pointed out that charges have not yet been framed in the case and, consequently, prosecution witnesses are yet to be examined. The court also noted that the charges were yet to be framed.Pais further submitted that a Special Leave Petition (SLP) is pending before the Supreme Court and that the trial court has indicated it would await the Supreme Court’s order. He then continued his submissions by referring to the Supreme Court judgment.Khalid and Imam had approached the Delhi High Court earlier this year after their bail applications were dismissed by the trial court for the third time on July 4. Imam was arrested in the case on August 25, 2020, while Khalid was arrested on September 13, 2020.The Delhi Police has opposed their bail pleas in the high court, asserting that the two were “masterminds” of the riots, PTI reported.The police argued that they could not seek bail on parity with other co-accused, stating that the Supreme Court had earlier categorised them as being part of the “command authority” and held that their “risk profiles” justified “continuing detention”.The police also argued that the present bail pleas were in the teeth of the Supreme Court’s January 5 order, which directed them to seek release only after the examination of protected witnesses was completed or after one year, whichever was earlier.On July 4, the trial court rejected Khalid’s bail application, saying it had “no option but to follow” the Supreme Court’s January 5 order and could therefore neither entertain the plea nor grant him relief.On September 2, 2025, a Delhi High Court division bench denied bail to Khalid and Imam. The Supreme Court upheld the verdict on January 5 but granted relief to co-accused Gulfisha Fatima, Meeran Haider, Shifa Ur Rehman, Mohammad Saleem Khan and Shadab Ahmad.A bench of Justice Aravind Kumar and Justice NV Anjaria had observed that there was a prima facie case against Khalid and Imam under the UAPA.On May 22, the Supreme Court granted six months’ interim bail to co-accused Abdul Khalid Saifi and Tasleem Ahmad, while referring to a larger bench the issue of prolonged incarceration of undertrials under the UAPA due to the stringent conditions for granting bail.
Article Summary: Delhi High Court refuses to grant bail to Umar Khalid and Sharjeel Imam in the UAPA case related to the 2020 Delhi riots. Delhi Police has opposed their bail pleas in the high court, asserting that the two were “masterminds” of the riots.

Flydubai pilot Captain Smit Machchhar spoke to Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu where he described the incidents that unfolded inside the cockpit. He also described how he managed to open the cockpit door despite suffering repeated blows to his head. Netanyahu praised his courage and said he had "saved so many souls".Machchhar told Netanyahu that the flight had initially been normal. The co-pilot then wanted to play a game that he said many locals play. While Machchhar was looking towards the front of the aircraft, he suddenly felt a heavy blow to the back of his head.Machchhar also told Netanyahu that the co-pilot had wanted to pray before the attack. He said he looked towards the front of the cockpit out of respect while the co-pilot prayed."...while he was praying, out of respect, I was just looking at the front and not at the back, and suddenly, after, I would say about four-five minutes, there was a big blow to the back of my head."My first thought was that there was a catastrophic damage to the aircraft and something is not right," Machchhar said.He said the blows continued and he soon realised that the aircraft had not been damaged. Instead, the co-pilot was attacking him."And that's when I realised that it's not the aircraft, it's the other guy who was in the cockpit with me," he said.Machchhar said the initial blows left his vision severely blurred, making it difficult for him to understand what was happening. He then felt the aircraft sharply descending."My memory is still in bits and pieces right now," he told Netanyahu.The pilot also recalled trying to open the cockpit door once, but said the co-pilot shut it again. He later found himself lying on the cockpit floor as he heard the aircraft moving rapidly and passengers screaming.Machchhar said he then realised he had to make one final attempt to reach the door."And as I was telling the ambassador here, that I had that one last fight left in me that, you know, call it personal or call it for people," he said. "But let's say I did it that if I don't do it, I'm going to die."He said he pushed himself towards the door and managed to open it. Crew members and others outside then took control of the situation."And thankfully people were waiting to bounce back, took over the control and the rest is what you know, sir," Machchhar said.Netanyahu asked Machchhar how he had managed to open the cockpit door when the co-pilot was preventing access.Machchhar explained that the door has a twist mechanism on the inside and can normally be opened from outside only using a code. His colleagues outside the cockpit were trying to enter the code, but the attacker was preventing the door from being opened."The only way to open the door was to reach the knob and like any other knob, just to twist it open and it opens on its own," Machchhar said."There is no pin, but yes, the door, it was, it was a short, quick twist, but the point was to reach to that point, to reach to that place."Once he reached the knob, Machchhar said he was able to twist it open.Netanyahu repeatedly praised Machchhar during the conversation, calling him a hero of India, Israel and the world."I, frankly, I'm amazed at your courage, at your coolness of judgement under impossible conditions," Netanyahu said.He said Machchhar's actions had helped save lives and described the incident as an example of how courage could overcome violence."You're a hero of Israel. You're a hero of India. You're a hero of the entire world," Netanyahu said.The Israeli prime minister also said Machchhar would be welcomed in Israel and invited him and his family to visit.Netanyahu said he wanted Machchhar and PM Modi to light a celebratory flame at Israel's next Independence Day ceremony. He described the honour as one usually reserved for Israeli citizens."I really would like them to bear a celebratory flame. It's our highest honour that we give in our Independence Day. It's usually reserved for Israeli citizens," Netanyahu said."But I think here in this case, all the citizens of Israel will, will embrace you. They do now and they will then too."Machchhar thanked Netanyahu and said he looked forward to meeting him in Israel.Netanyahu ended the conversation by wishing the pilot a speedy recovery and saying his visit to Israel would be "memorable and historic".
Article Summary: Flydubai pilot Captain Smit Machchhar spoke to Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu. He described the incidents that unfolded inside the cockpit. Article Title: Congress resets Team Uttar Pradesh: 5 clear messages for BJP and Akhilesh Yadav
Article Text:
Congress replaced Ajay Rai with Aradhana Misra Mona as Uttar Pradesh Congress chief.

1. A bigger, but amicable, say at seat-sharing table

What Mona Misra said after her appointment as UP Congress chief

2. Rebuilding old social reach, but with a new mix

What Ajay Rai said after being replaced as UP Congress chief

3. Not conceding Muslim vote

What Imran Masood said after UP Congress organizational reshuffle

4. Congress wants credibility

5. Women power at heart

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: Congress has overhauled its Uttar Pradesh organisation ahead of the 2027 assembly election, replacing Ajay Rai with three-time Rampur Khas MLA Aradhana Misra Mona as state unit president and appointing Saharanpur MP Imran Masood as working president. The party has also named Chaudhary Virendra Singh as Congress legislature party leader.The reshuffle brings together a prominent Brahmin leader from eastern UP, a Muslim leader with influence in western UP, and Dalit and OBC representation in senior organisational positions. Rajendra Pal Gautam, a Dalit leader, is already the party's Uttar Pradesh in-charge. With these recent appointments, Congress may be trying to widen its social and regional reach after years of electoral decline in the state.Taken together, the appointments suggest that Congress is trying to do two things at once: strengthen its bargaining position with the Samajwadi Party while rebuilding an independent political identity in Uttar Pradesh.The timing is important. The 2024 Lok Sabha election revived Congress's presence in UP through its alliance with Akhilesh Yadav . But Akhilesh’s party remains the much larger organisation in the state. In the 2024 polls, SP moved 32 seats up and won 37 seats, registering a 15.73% gain in vote share.On the other hand, Congress also slightly improved its Lok Sabha tally with 6 seats and a jump of a little over 3% vote share.Congress is now trying to turn that electoral revival into a more substantial organisational base before the 2027 assembly election in a state which has been long associated with Congress's political success story.Here are the five messages embedded in the reset.The appointment of Aradhana Misra Mona as UPCC president, along with the elevation of Imran Masood, suggests that Congress wants to push for a larger share of assembly seats while keeping its relationship with the Samajwadi Party workable.Masood has been unusually vocal about Congress' seat demand. On September 3, he argued that if Congress' electoral performance continued to improve, its share of seats should also increase."Hum koi bhikhari hain jo Samajwadi Party se bheekh mangenge? ... Party formula tay karegi, lekin jo formula Lok Sabha election mein tha, woh formula nahi hoga. (Are we beggars who will beg from Samajwadi Party? ... The party will decide the formula, but it will not be the same formula used in the Lok Sabha elections)," he had told ANI.Congress' UP in-charge Rajendra Pal Gautam has also spoken of seeking an equal number of seats with the SP, while Masood has backed a 50:50 formula.The rhetoric sharpened on September 28, when Masood directly declared: "If Akhilesh Yadav is unhappy (with seat-sharing discussion), the loss will be his own... We fail to understand what the anger is even about."Mona's elevation, on the other hand, sends a somewhat different signal. Unlike the more combative rhetoric around seat-sharing, her appointment gives Congress a state president who is seen as having a more workable equation with the SP leadership. Her political experience and close association with the Congress leadership also give her a role in managing the alliance even as the party pushes for greater space.The numbers give Congress some basis for making that argument. In the 2024 Lok Sabha election, the SP won 37 of UP's 80 seats while Congress won six, taking the INDIA bloc's combined tally to 43. The SP's 37-seat tally was a dramatic rise from five seats in 2019.However, going by the numbers, Congress cannot negotiate from the position of higher power and will most likely have to settle for the junior partner role.But how "small" the partner role it gets will be crucial.One of the clearest messages in the new team is social and regional balancing.Mona is a prominent Brahmin face from eastern Uttar Pradesh. Masood brings a prominent Muslim face from western UP. Devinder Nishad gives the organisation an OBC, riverine-community face, while Alok Prasad brings Dalit representation into the senior state team. Rajendra Pal Gautam is already the party's Dalit in-charge for Uttar Pradesh.The choice of Mona is particularly significant because she replaces Ajay Rai, a Bhumihar leader, with another upper-caste leader from a different community. The switch from Rai to Mona could be read as an attempt to reconnect with Brahmin voters who were traditionally associated with Congress but have, over time, moved substantially towards the BJP.This rejig comes at a time when the upper-caste groups (Rajputs, Brahmins, Tyagis) reportedly feel increasingly sidelined by BJP's aggressive outreach toward non-Yadav OBC and Dalit vote banks. Tensions stem from ticket distribution cuts, perceived administrative favour toward Rajputs over Brahmins, and farmers' issues.Mona's appointment, however, is not simply a return to Congress's old social formula. The new team combines upper-caste, Muslim, Dalit and OBC representation, while also distributing the leadership geographically between eastern and western UP.The BJP has built a broad social coalition of its own in Uttar Pradesh. Congress' organisational response now appears to be an attempt to create multiple social entry points into the party rather than rely on a single caste or community bloc.Masood's elevation carries another particularly important message for western Uttar Pradesh.The Saharanpur MP is one of Congress' most prominent Muslim leaders in the state, and his appointment puts a western UP Muslim face in the second-most important position in the state organisation. His appointment seems to be a direct attempt to attract and consolidate Muslim support.That matters because the SP has traditionally been the principal opposition party competing for the Muslim vote in UP. The 2024 Lok Sabha election demonstrated the strength of that relationship.A post-election CSDS-Lokniti analysis estimated that 77% of Muslim respondents in Uttar Pradesh voted for the SP and 15% for Congress, while 2% reported voting for the BJP. These are, of course, survey estimates and not absolute vote counts. However, it may reflect the trend.The actual election results also showed the importance of Muslim-heavy constituencies to the opposition's performance. Congress won Saharanpur and Sitapur, while the SP and its allies captured several other such seats.Masood's promotion therefore gives Congress a prominent vehicle to seek Muslim support directly rather than relying entirely on the SP to bring that constituency into the alliance.Mona's appointment is significant because she brings an electoral record to the top of the state unit.She first entered the Uttar Pradesh assembly through a bypoll in 2014 and subsequently retained Rampur Khas in the 2017 and 2022 elections. She has therefore won the seat three times. Before entering the assembly, she served as block pramukh of Sangramgarh from 2002 to 2014 and held positions in the organisation and cooperative sector.Her 2022 victory was particularly notable because Congress was reduced to just two assembly seats across Uttar Pradesh. She defeated BJP's Nagesh Pratap Singh by 14,741 votes, polling 84,334 votes, or 50.27%, according to Election Commission data.That gives Congress a state president who is not merely an organisational appointee but an incumbent with a repeated assembly-winning record.The appointment of Aradhana Misra Mona also gives Congress a prominent woman at the helm of its Uttar Pradesh organisation, at a time when BJP too is putting renewed emphasis on its women leaders in the state.The timing is notable. The BJP has recently brought back Smriti Irani into a more prominent organisational role, signalling that women leaders continue to have an important place in its political strategy. Irani, who beat Rahul Gandhi and represented Amethi in the Lok Sabha from 2019 to 2024, remains one of the BJP's most recognisable women faces in Uttar Pradesh.The Mona-Priyanka Gandhi combination will give Congress a big women power picture it can easily put on its posters.The wider electoral numbers also underline why women matter. In the 2024 Lok Sabha election, the Election Commission recorded female voter turnout in Uttar Pradesh at 57.22%, compared with 56.46% among men. Women therefore turned out at a slightly higher rate than men in the state.As a bonus, Mona's elevation also gives Congress a combination of representation and political substance: a woman leader, a Brahmin face, a three-time assembly winner and someone with an established organisational network.The new UP team combines experience with caste, community, regional and gender representation, giving Congress multiple entry points in the voter base. The real test now will be whether the reshuffle can translate into stronger grassroots organisation and enough bargaining power ahead of the 2027 assembly election.
Article Summary: Congress replaced Ajay Rai with Aradhana Misra Mona as Uttar Pradesh Congress chief. The party has also named Chaudhary Virendra Singh as Congress legislature party leader. The reshuffle brings together a prominent Brahmin leader from eastern UP, a Muslim leader with influence in western UP.

Article Title: 'AAP asked you not to': Congress leader claims CJP refused party's help during Assam detention
Article Text:
Congress, CJP spar over Assam outreach

'You asked us to stay out of it'

'Sidelined Neha Bora'

Row follows Ranka's criticism

NEW DELHI: Congress spokesperson Reetam Singh has claimed that Cockroach Janta Party (CJP) co-convenor Ashutosh Ranka refused to meet Congress leaders during his recent Assam visit. He alleged that the group was told to stay away because its outreach was "an Aam Aadmi Party initiative".Singh's response came after Ashutosh Ranka and Saurav Das called out a fake "liberal ecosystem", saying that they believed they were alone responsible for “saving India, saving constitution”. However, they did not name Congress directly.Singh made the allegation in a post on X on Saturday while responding to Ranka, who had criticised what he described as an “entire ‘self-declared liberal’ ecosystem” targeting CJP founder Abhijeet Dipke.Singh said Congress workers had helped CJP members after they were detained by Assam Police and claimed that Ranka nevertheless declined a courtesy meeting with Congress leaders, including Assam Congress president Gaurav Gogoi.This comes days after Ranka and more than 40 CJP volunteers were detained in Guwahati ahead of a regional volunteers' meeting. Opposition parties, including Congress, AAP, the Assam Jatiya Parishad and Raijor Dal, had criticised the police action.Addressing Ranka, Singh said Congress members had helped secure the release of CJP workers after their detention.“When you were detained by Assam Police. We, Congress people helped to get CJP people out. Yet you categorically refused to have even a courtesy meeting with our Congress leaders and Gaurav Sir,” Singh said."You refused it because the Aam Aadmi Party asked you to not to. Kunki Chowdhury who was your Host in Guwahati, was on Election Campaign with AJP President Lurin Gogoi Da for a Congress Candidate in Nagaon. Even they had asked you to meet and discuss with Congress. Yet not once, you chose to engage with Congress or our students wing. You asked us to stay out of it. And that it is a Aam Aadmi Party initiative," he added.Singh also referred to Kunki Chowdhury, at whose residence Ranka and other CJP members were reportedly detained. He claimed Chowdhury had asked Ranka to meet Congress leaders and discuss the group's activities.CJP members had been detained from the residence of Assam Jatiya Parishad leader Kunki Chowdhury in the Dispur area ahead of their scheduled meeting.Singh further accused Ranka and CJP of trying to portray the movement as an AAP initiative and referred to the group's earlier protests in Delhi.“We know how you sidelined Neha Bora in the Jantar Mantar 1.0 protests and when even Left chose to engage with our Leader Rahul Gandhi Ji. You decided you will not engage under direct instructions of Arvind Kejriwal,” he said.He also alleged that AAP had previously sought to associate itself with movements led by others, citing the India Against Corruption movement and activist Sonam Wangchuk's protest.“Aam Aadmi Party is known for piggy riding and hijacking issues of others,” Singh said.Singh said CJP was “a people's movement” and argued that it should not be treated as the property of any political party.“Let us keep it civil and issue centric. The cause is bigger than a political party,” he said.“CJP is a decentralised movement. There is no one Supreme Leader or his hierarchy. We all are equals. That is why people support it.”Ranka's post that triggered Singh's response had accused a “self-declared liberal” group of targeting Dipke and questioning his growing reach.“An entire “self-declared liberal” ecosystem has been activated to denounce @abhijeet_dipke and the fact that he has been able to capture the imagination of millions of Indians after a LONG LONG time,” Ranka said.CJP co-convenor Saurav Das also criticised what he described as a group from outside the BJP that believed it alone was responsible for “saving India, saving constitution”. Neither Ranka nor Das named a political party in their posts."It’s a very big problem. A certain section—not just the BJP—another party thinks “saving India, saving constitution” is only their job. They are self-declared liberals and self-declared thekedars of the constitution," he said."It’s a very salty ecosystem, acting worse than the BJP’s ecosystem sometimes. They must realise that they can’t divide and rule through such tactics. Their massive failures over the years has led us to this moment where the young have to show the way. So they should just zip it on us and focus on how to support the young! Total buffoons!" he added.The latest exchange has brought CJP's political affiliations and its relationship with opposition parties into focus, even as the organisation continues its outreach on issues including education and electoral rolls.
Article Summary: Congress spokesperson Reetam Singh claims Cockroach Janta Party (CJP) co- convenor Ashutosh Ranka refused to meet Congress leaders during his recent Assam visit. He alleged that the group was told to stay away because its outreach was "an Aam Aadmi Party initiative"

Article Title: ‘He was so scared’: SP MP on ally Rahul Gandhi skipping Amethi in 2024 Lok Sabha polls
Article Text:
"Rahul Gandhi was reluctant to contest the 2024 Lok Sabha election from Amethi," says Congress ally.

Patel credits SP for Congress wins

SP MP dismisses Congress's caste strategy

Congress hits back

NEW DELHI: Strain deepened within the Samajwadi Party-Congress alliance ahead of Uttar Pradesh polls, with SP MP Shiv Pal Singh Patel in an off-the-cuff remark claimed that Rahul Gandhi was "reluctant to contest the 2024 Lok Sabha election" from Amethi and chose Raebareli because he was "so scared".Patel, who represents Pratapgarh, also credited the SP-Congress alliance for the Congress's six Lok Sabha wins in Uttar Pradesh, arguing that the party would have drawn a blank in the state without SP's support.Speaking to news agency PTI, Patel said the SP leadership had to persuade Gandhi to contest from Raebareli after he appeared unwilling to fight from Amethi, the traditional Gandhi family constituency."Had there been no alliance (with the Samajwadi Party ), they (Congress) wouldn't have won a single seat. It even reached a point where their top leader Rahul Gandhi was ready to give up his seat. He contested from elsewhere (Raebareli) instead of Amethi. He was so scared," he said.The leader futher added: "It was our national president who reassured and persuaded him, asking him to contest and warning that if he didn't, he (Akhilesh) would field his own candidate. Only then did Gandhi agree to contest. Otherwise, he was extremely reluctant to run for that traditional seat, the one said to belong to the Nehru family.Gandhi only managed to win it because of that persuasion," he said.Patel said SP voters backed Congress candidates in constituencies allotted to the Congress under the alliance arrangement."Every single vote from the Samajwadi Party went to the Congress wherever they were allotted seats. That is precisely how they managed to win those six seats," he said.The SP won 37 of Uttar Pradesh's 80 Lok Sabha seats in the 2024 elections, while Congress won six. The BJP won 33 seats, while the NDA's tally in the state stood at 36.Patel said the difference in the two parties' performances should be reflected in any future seat-sharing discussions."We secured 37 seats. We are far ahead of the Congress in every respect. They shouldn't ask for more than 50, and should feel happy. The Congress should cooperate, rather than making all sorts of absurd or negative remarks," Patel said.Patel also criticised the Congress's reported caste strategy in Uttar Pradesh, including its appointment of a Brahmin as state Congress president and a Muslim as working president."This will not yield any benefit. Look, Dalits were with Mayawati, but they have now shifted to our side. They realised that there was no significant upliftment of Dalits during the Congress regime, and certainly none is happening under the BJP. Whereas, during the Samajwadi Party's tenure, everyone gets equal opportunities. Everyone gets an equal chance to progress; their children get a chance to receive an education. "He added, "That is precisely why the party was named 'Samajwadi'. Our party operates based on the ideals of (Ram Manohar) Lohia-ji. Our party's objective is the welfare of all sections of society."The SP currently has 101 MLAs in the 403-member Uttar Pradesh Assembly, while Congress has two.Patel said the SP could benefit from continuing its alliance with Congress, but argued that the Congress would suffer more if it contested elections without its regional ally."If we proceed with an alliance, we will certainly benefit. Even if it doesn't happen, we won't have any significant loss. But for them, the tally will drop to zero. I can say this with confidence: if they don't contest as part of an alliance, they will end up with zero seats.The public will realise they are fielding candidates solely to split votes. If they act as vote-spoilers, they will be reduced to zero," Patel said.Uttar Pradesh Congress spokesperson Anshu Awasthi pushed back against Patel's remarks and said the SP should rein in leaders making such statements."The Samajwadi Party must work to rein in leaders who make such statements. It is because of the INDIA bloc that he (Patel) has become an MP. He should know his limits and avoid making statements like these," Awasthi told PTI.
Article Summary: SP MP Shiv Pal Singh Patel claims Rahul Gandhi was "reluctant to contest the 2024 Lok Sabha election" from Amethi. Patel also credited the SP-Congress alliance for the Congress's six Lok Sabha wins in Uttar Pradesh. Patel said the SP leadership had to persuade Gandhi to contest from Raebareli.

NEW DELHI: Delhi environment minister Manjinder Singh Sirsa on Saturday hit out at the Punjab government over the killing of makeup artist and social media influencer Mad Sandhu, alleging that the state’s law and order was in the hands of the “mafia”.Sandhu, whose real name was Madhusudan, was shot dead by two unidentified motorcycle-borne men on Loharka Road in Amritsar at around 6pm on Saturday. Police said the attackers opened fire before fleeing the spot.Sandhu suffered two gunshot wounds and was rushed to a private hospital in critical condition, where he later died during treatment. An eyewitness said around two to three rounds were fired and that Sandhu was shot at close range.Reacting to the killing, Sirsa questioned the law and order situation in Punjab and alleged that several criminal networks were operating in the state under the Aam Aadmi Party government.“There is no law and order in Punjab. The law and order situation in Punjab is in the hands of the mafia. In Punjab, you receive only one piece of information every day,” Sirsa told ANI.“Otherwise, the police do not even register an FIR. If they are drug dealers, they are going around killing people. If they are mafia members, they are killing people. If there are gangsters, they are killing people. Social media influencer Mad Sandhu was shot dead and if even the Sarpanch of a village is not safe, and a former Sarpanch is not safe, then who is safe?”Sirsa further alleged that extortion gangs, mafia groups and the drug mafia were operating in Punjab.“During the tenure of the Aam Aadmi Party, gangs involved in extortion, the mafia, and the drug mafia are operating in Punjab. There is also a school mafia operating, where even if you raise your voice against problems in schools, you will be thrown out of the party,” he added.Madhusudan Sandhu was a makeup artist and social media influencer who regularly appeared on podcasts and digital platforms, where he spoke about make-up artistry, the film industry and gender issues. His content and fashion choices had also attracted criticism and abuse on social media.Sandhu had around 2.26 lakh followers on Instagram and had acted in the Punjabi film *Oye Bhole Oye*. A few months ago, a Nihang Sikh had objected to his social media content and clothing, saying his videos could have a negative impact on young people.Congress leader Raj Kumar Verka also criticised the AAP government over the killing and demanded Punjab Chief Minister Bhagwant Mann’s resignation, alleging that the government had failed to protect people.Amritsar MP Gurjeet Singh Aujla said Sandhu had been receiving threats for a long time and had spoken about them publicly on social media. He questioned why the threats had not been taken seriously and demanded an early arrest and a thorough investigation into who was behind the killing and why Sandhu had been threatened.
Article Summary: Madhusudan Sandhu was shot dead by two unidentified motorcycle-borne men on Loharka Road in Amritsar at around 6pm on Saturday. Delhi environment minister Manjinder Singh Sirsa hit out at the Punjab government over the killing. Sirsa alleged that several criminal networks were operating in the state under the Aam Aadmi Party government.

NEW DELHI: The Press Club of India has condemned the Delhi Police ’s alleged treatment of journalists and imposition of internet ban during protests at Jantar Mantar against chief election commissioner Gyanesh Kumar on Friday and Saturday, saying such behaviour “cannot be normalised in a democracy”.In a statement, the Press Club said it was “shocked and dismayed” by the police action against journalists covering the protests and raised concerns over media freedom in the national capital.“Journalists must be allowed to work freely, without fear, and document those who gather to raise various issues,” the Press Club said, adding that the restrictions on journalists even in the heart of Delhi “do not bode well for the trajectory of media freedom in India”.The Press Club also urged the Delhi Police to immediately act on a complaint filed by a female journalist and ensure that mediapersons are able to perform their duties without facing “aggression and threats”.Eearlier in the day, Delhi Police said it had received complaints from three female journalists alleging sexual harassment during a protest in the New Delhi area on October 3. Article Title: 'Most comprehensive plan': Ukraine confirms India playing role in mediating energy truce in Black Sea
Article Text:
File photo: Prime Minister Narendra Modi during a meeting with Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy (Picture credit: PTI)

India proposal among four initiatives

Kyiv backs safe Black Sea shipping

Also read:

Russia's position remains key to next steps

NEW DELHI: India's role in efforts to find a negotiated end to the Russia-Ukraine war has gained greater prominence, with Kyiv describing an Indian proposal as the most comprehensive among four initiatives currently under discussion and saying New Delhi has, for the first time, indicated its willingness to play an active mediating role.Ukrainian foreign minister Andrii Sybiha recently said Ukraine was prepared to consider both an energy and agricultural truce in the Black Sea, while also remaining open to an unconditional ceasefire along the line of contact."We have four proposals. The most comprehensive is India's proposal. For the first time, India has signalled its willingness to play a role," Sybiha said during a press briefing, according to RBC Ukraine.According to Sybiha, four proposals are currently being considered in diplomatic efforts surrounding the war.India's proposal was described by the Ukrainian foreign minister as the most comprehensive.Türkiye and Egypt have separately proposed a grain and agricultural truce in the Black Sea, while the United States has put forward an energy truce proposal.The agricultural and maritime component is particularly important for Egypt, which relies on Ukrainian grain for roughly a third of its supply, according to RBC Ukraine.The US proposal on an energy truce was also discussed during a meeting between Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy and US President Donald Trump.Kyiv has conveyed its own approach to its partners and wants the energy and Black Sea components to be treated as an interconnected package.Sybiha said the energy component would require a complete halt to attacks on energy infrastructure, including port facilities.Ukraine has also expressed readiness for an unconditional ceasefire along the line of contact. Sybiha said such a ceasefire could potentially emerge from a meeting between Zelenskyy and Russian President Vladimir Putin.The US is currently working actively on this diplomatic track, according to the Ukrainian foreign minister.The latest Ukrainian position builds on India's earlier engagement with Kyiv over restoring safe navigation in the Black Sea.During last month's UN General Assembly-related engagements, Zelenskyy said Egypt, India and Türkiye had put forward options for a maritime truce between Russia and Ukraine."We are waiting for Russia's response. Ukraine is ready ... to ensure safe shipping and food security in the Black Sea if Russia is ready to take real steps towards de-escalation too. We have to start somewhere," Zelenskyy said at the time.India has been engaging with both Moscow and Kyiv while advocating dialogue and diplomacy.External affairs minister S Jaishankar had said India was in continuous contact with both sides and was exploring ideas that could help mitigate and eventually end the conflict."If India can be of any help, in any manner, we are there," Jaishankar said during his visit to Kyiv last month.During that visit, Jaishankar met Zelenskyy and Sybiha, with discussions covering peace efforts, bilateral cooperation, Black Sea navigation and global food security.Sybiha had also said Ukraine valued India's engagement in efforts to restore freedom of navigation in the Black Sea."Restoring freedom of navigation is critical for global food security. Ukraine is ready to play a constructive role and we value India’s engagement," he said in a post on X.While Ukraine has indicated its readiness to consider multiple limited ceasefire arrangements, Russia's response remains central to whether the proposals can move forward.Sybiha's comments come amid differing assessments in Europe over Moscow's willingness to enter substantive peace negotiations.German Chancellor Friedrich Merz recently said Russia was not currently interested in genuine peace negotiations, while German foreign minister Johann Wadephul has expressed expectations that talks to end the war could begin in the near future.The Kremlin had previously said there were no prerequisites for moving towards a broader peace negotiating track while maintaining that Russia remained open to talks."For now, there are no prerequisites for moving on to a peaceful negotiating track, although we, as the Russian side, remain open to peace talks," Kremlin spokesman Dmitry Peskov said.Ukraine's latest position therefore places several limited ceasefire proposals, covering energy infrastructure, Black Sea shipping and agricultural supplies, alongside the possibility of a broader unconditional ceasefire along the line of contact.India's proposal is being considered alongside those initiatives, with Sybiha describing it as the most comprehensive and saying New Delhi has now signalled its readiness to play a role in the process.
Article Summary: India's proposal is described by the Ukrainian foreign minister as the most comprehensive. Türkiye and Egypt have separately proposed a grain and agricultural truce in the Black Sea. The United States has put forward an energy truce proposal. Russia's response remains central to whether the proposals can move forward.

Article Title: Delhi landfill garbage mountains shrinking, 100 acres reclaimed in 18 months: CM Rekha Gupta
Article Text:
Delhi CM Rekha Gupta poses for a group picture during an on-site inspection of waste disposal operations near Okhla, in New Delhi

Government targets legacy and fresh waste

New processing plants at three sites

Poll Vote & Share your view What is your top concern regarding pollution in Delhi? Landfill waste Air quality Water quality (Yamuna) Dust pollution 3k+ users shared opinion today 5k+ users already voted today 3k+ users shared opinion today Share Opinion

Focus on pollution and waste management

NEW DELHI: Delhi chief minister Rekha Gupta on Saturday said the garbage mountains at the city's landfill sites were steadily shrinking as she reviewed waste disposal work at Okhla and laid the foundation stone for new waste processing facilities at Okhla, Ghazipur and Singhola.Gupta said the Delhi government had reclaimed 100 acres of land across the city's three landfill sites over the past one-and-a-half years, with a large portion of the cleared area also being turned green.She said almost all legacy waste at Okhla that existed before January 2025 had been processed."Today, at Okhla, we have processed almost all the legacy waste that was there before January 2025," Gupta said.Gupta said the government was working on two fronts: clearing the existing garbage mountains while ensuring that fresh waste generated every day did not accumulate into new landfill sites.According to news agency ANI, she said around 3,000-4,000 metric tonnes of fresh waste reaches the sites daily and is being processed round the clock."The garbage currently piled up here is essentially fresh waste generated after January 2025, and that too is being processed round the clock. So, we are fighting on two fronts: one is eliminating waste, and the other is ensuring that the 3,000 to 4,000 metric tons of fresh waste arriving daily is processed immediately, so that new garbage mountains are not formed for future generations," Gupta said.She said the government was working to reduce the existing garbage mountains to zero."People are seeing that the garbage mountains are continuously shrinking and soon a time will come when they will become zero," Gupta said.Gupta also said she had taken what she described as her "last selfie" with the garbage mountain at Okhla."Today I have taken my last selfie with the garbage mountain; after this I have taken a pledge that this garbage mountain will end soon," she said.Taking a jibe at the Opposition, Gupta added, "I had said - garbage mountain, you will have to go; the opposition mocked. Today I will say the garbage mountain is going; now only its back remains."During the programme at the Okhla SLF site, Gupta laid the foundation stone for fresh waste processing plants at Okhla, Ghazipur and Singhola, as well as a biogas facility at Ghazipur. She also inaugurated the M&CW Centre at Kotla Mubarakpur through virtual mode from Okhla.The Okhla plant will be built at a cost of Rs 103 crore and will have a processing capacity of 1,400 metric tonnes per day.The Singhola facility will cost Rs 42 crore and have a capacity of 800 metric tonnes per day, while the Ghazipur plant will have a processing capacity of 700 metric tonnes per day.The facilities are intended to process fresh waste as well as construction and demolition waste. Gupta said the new units would also produce biogas, green energy and manure."Waste should not remain waste; Delhi should use it as wealth," she said, adding that new technologies were being introduced for waste segregation and processing.She said waste and cattle dung would be used to produce biogas and manure as part of efforts to build a technology-driven waste management system.Gupta said the government was taking up several measures to address pollution, including work on landfill waste, cleaning the Yamuna, dust mitigation, plantation, road infrastructure and waste management."Our government is tackling pollution from a 360-degree perspective to ensure it gradually decreases. We are working on every aspect, be it addressing the mountains of garbage, cleaning the Yamuna, improving road infrastructure, or managing waste, to ensure the people of Delhi enjoy better air quality. Our resolve and policies are absolutely clear, and we are working 24x7 in the public interest," she said.The chief minister also reviewed the progress of waste disposal work with officials and directed them to accelerate the work according to the stipulated timeline.She said the garbage mountains at Bhalswa, Ghazipur and Okhla had caused inconvenience to people travelling through these areas and said the government was continuing efforts to eliminate them.
Article Summary: Gupta said the Delhi government had reclaimed 100 acres of land across the city's three landfill sites over the past one-and-a-half years. She said almost all legacy waste at Okhla that existed before January 2025 had been processed. Gupta said the new units would also produce biogas, green energy and manure.

Article Title: Watch: Netanyahu invites PM Modi, pilot Smit Machchhar to Israel I-Day event
Article Text:
Netanyahu praised the pilot for his actions during the incident and hailed him as 'hero of the entire world'.

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

Flydubai co-pilot attacked captain with crash axe

Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu has invited Prime Minister Narendra Modi and Indian pilot Captain Smit Machchhar to light a flame at Israel's Independence Day event. Speaking to Machchhar, he called him a "hero" of Israel, India and the entire world for foiling an alleged attempt to crash an Israel-bound flydubai flight.Netanyahu spoke to the 38-year-old pilot on Saturday while Machchhar was undergoing treatment at a hospital in the UAE. During the emotional conversation, Machchhar recounted how he was attacked by his co-pilot inside the cockpit and revealed new details about the incident."It's our highest honour that we give on our Independence Day. It's usually reserved for Israeli citizens, but I think here in this case, all the citizens of Israel will embrace you. They do now, and they will then too. So we hope to see you very soon in Israel," Netanyahu told Machchhar.The Israeli Prime Minister's office later said on X, "You are a hero for Israel, India, and the entire world. I invite Prime Minister Narendra Modi and you to light a flame on Israeli Independence Day.""During the emotional conversation that took place this evening, the Prime Minister asked Captain Machchhar how it all started, and Machchhar revealed new details about the terrifying moments in the cockpit," the post said.Machchhar told Netanyahu that the co-pilot had wanted to pray before the attack. He said he looked towards the front of the cockpit out of respect while the co-pilot prayed."...while he was praying, out of respect, I was just looking at the front and not at the back, and suddenly, after, I would say about four-five minutes, there was a big blow to the back of my head."My first thought was that there was catastrophic damage to the aircraft and something was not right. But then after that, the blows kept coming one after the other, and that's when I realised that it's not the aircraft, it's the other guy who was in the cockpit with me," Machchhar said.Netanyahu praised the pilot for his actions during the incident."You saved so many souls. I think you saved something bigger. You saved the spirit of the world...It's something that is being justly hailed around the world. You're a hero of Israel. You're a hero of India. You're a hero of the entire world," Netanyahu told Machchhar."You know, I guess it's a twist of fate, and a twist of faith, and what you did is remarkable. I heard, of course, from the Israeli passengers what transpired after that, and you're a great hero, and you were accompanied by heroes, and you saved the day," he said.Netanyahu also told Machchhar he was "amazed at his courage" and "at your coolness of judgment under impossible conditions."The incident took place on Wednesday aboard flydubai flight FZ1073, which was carrying 174 passengers to Israel. Machchhar was allegedly attacked by his co-pilot with a crash axe, an emergency tool kept inside the cockpit.The aircraft transmitted emergency signals and made a rapid descent of more than 17,000 feet, from 34,000 feet. It eventually made an emergency landing in Saudi Arabia. The descent was so extreme that part of the aircraft's rudder was reportedly torn away.The co-pilot has been identified as Omani national Hamam al-Hammami, according to a Wall Street Journal report citing people familiar with the matter.Machchhar received initial treatment in Tabuk before being shifted to Abu Dhabi for continued medical care.The co-pilot of a Flydubai flight, Hamam al-Hammami, allegedly attacked the captain with a crash axe inside the cockpit and attempted to take control of the aircraft. UAE described the incident as a terrorist attack.UAE prosecutor general Hamad Saif Al Shamsi said the co-pilot launched the attack during Wednesday's flight and tried to seize control of the aircraft. The incident was subsequently classified by UAE authorities as an attempted terrorist attack.
Article Summary: Netanyahu spoke to the 38-year-old pilot on Saturday while Machchhar was undergoing treatment at a hospital in the UAE. He called him a "hero" of Israel, India and the entire world for foiling an alleged attempt to crash an Israel- bound flydubai flight. Israeli Prime Minister's office later said, "I invite Prime Minister Narendra Modi and you to light a flame on Israeli Independence Day"

Court steps in over library's future
